query: Correction for multiple testing was done using permutation based FDR (Fehrmann et al., 2011). Subject labels were permuted 1000 times and associations were computed using the permuted data (all biological aging indicators vs all health determinants). For each of the observed p-values (p) the FDR was computed as the average number of permuted p-values smaller than p, divided by the amount of real p-values smaller than p, resulting in a p-value threshold of 2e-2 for a FDR of 5% for all tests.
